walkthroughs.body_html: Annual sources include fossil fuels (around 9.5 GtC), land use change (around 1 GtC), totalling around 10.5 GtC. Sinks: land takes around 3 GtC, ocean around 2.8 GtC. The remainder (around 4.7 GtC) stays in the atmosphere. Tracking each component lets us measure progress toward net zero.

The Earth carbon balance: Atmospheric change = sources - sinks. Inserting recent values: Change = 10.5 - 5.8 = 4.7 GtC per year stays airborne. Multiplied by 3.67 converts to 17.2 Gt CO2 per year accumulating, raising atmospheric CO2 by around 2.3 ppm annually.

Mass of CO2 = mass of C x (44 / 12) = 3.67. Emit 1 GtC and 3.67 Gt CO2 enters the atmosphere. So global emissions of around 10 GtC equal around 37 Gt CO2 per year. Always check which unit a chart uses; mixing them is a common exam trap.
